content.title: Official Blind Review #4
content.review:
This paper provide certification of the adversarial robustness of graph-based laplacian semi-supervised learning under evasion attacks with $l_2$ norm considered. The authors provide detailed theoretical justification on their main result of $\delta$-robustness with reasonable assumptions. Theoretically, the authors prove that GL-based classifier is more robust than KNN-based classifier under the assumptions made. Empirical experimental results also support their findings. Overall, I believe this paper provide some good contributions in understanding the robustness of GL-based SSL.

My questions:
- section 1.1 and 5: if the authors mention that their results can provide some feasible explanation of using GL-based activation function to improve DNNs' robustness, it would be good to see at least some sentences to discuss it in the paper instead of just briefly mentioning it in your contributions and conclusions.
- section 2.1: why is the graph laplacian defined between (A3) and (A4) in the form of $\sum W_{x,y} (u(x) - u(y))$? The graph Dirichlet energy defined at the beginning of section 1 is in the form of $\sum W_{x,y} (u(x) - u(y))^2$, which I believe is correct. If no square on $(u(x) - u(y))$, does it really relate to laplacian of $W_{x,y}$? Or is there anything I missed about dropping the square sign? Also, same definition of graph laplacian is used when proving the last inequality of Lemma A.7. My first thought tells me this lemma is still provable if we have ^2 on $(u(x) - u(y))$. Please either check it carefully or clarify my confusion.
- minor comments: some sentences are a bit hard to understand during my first read of this paper, probably due to grammar errors? Better check it carefully.
content.confidence: 3: The reviewer is fairly confident that the evaluation is correct

display_title: Work in progress needing better presentation and experimental evaluation

content.title: Work in progress needing better presentation and experimental evaluation
content.review:
The paper is a theoretical analysis of adversarial robustness of Graph Laplacian based semi-supervised learning. 

Pros:

+ The paper addresses an important problem of adversarial robustness by exploiting unlabeled data. It studies the theoretical robustness of graph Laplacian approach. 

Cons:

- The attack model is not very well motivated and connected to some realistic situations. The adversary is assumed to be able to corrupt the unlabeled data by moving each point a maximum distance of r in `L2-norm. It would help to have a motivation for this attacker model. It seems to be a strange model which is less powerful than typical poisoning/Trojan-injection attacks but also in a sense very powerful requiring all unlabeled data to be moved. This raises the concern that is the problem being defined to fit a particular technique rather than vice versa. While previous work in Wang 2018b can be viewed as a motivation, it would help to discuss why this problem is important in the paper directly. 

- The disconnect between the use of the geometric random graph construction in A4 and kNN in the experiments does not appear to be just a minor technical issue. The conjecture in Remark 2.3 needs better justification. 

- The theoretical results are a direct application of results from Calder (2018) which further raises concern that the definition of the problem is motivated by some practical value or designed to fit the results from Calder. 

- The experiments have been run on very simple benchmarks. Given the higher computational complexity of the GL approach, this raises a concern that the presented approach would not be applicable for reasonably complex datasets where one would possibly need relatively higher values of k. 

Questions to the authors:

It will be helpful to the reviewer to better understand the theoretical novelty if the concerns listed above can be clarified.  

In summary, this appears to be interesting and promising direction of research.  But in its current form, the paper appears to be a work in progress requiring better distillation of theoretical novelty and convincing experimental evaluation.
content.rating: 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection
content.confidence: 4: The reviewer is confident but not absolutely certain that the evaluation is correct

display_title: This paper presents a way to show that the semi-supervised Laplacian regression is provably robust to l-2 norm attacks under certain assumptions.

content.title: This paper presents a way to show that the semi-supervised Laplacian regression is provably robust to l-2 norm attacks under certain assumptions.
content.review:
This paper presents a way to show that the semi-supervised Laplacian regression is provably robust to l-2 norm attacks excursively on the feature space. The main message is, under some assumptions, semi-supervised Laplacian regression is naturally robust to l-2 norm attacks (on the features). The Laplacian regression approach is compared with KNN on 3 datasets for classification tasks.

While Laplacian regression is indeed a useful machine learning algorithm, there seems to be a mismatch between the attack model and the application scenarios.  Typically, Laplacian regression should be applied if there is a graphical structure in the data. For example, in a recommendation system where users and items can be viewed as nodes and an edge between a user and an item implies a user may like this item. Thus, a natural attack would be related to the graph structure: such as removing, adding, or modifying an edge. But this paper only considers attacking feature vectors but not edges. This does seem to be wired considering the nature of the problem. Technically, ignoring the edge attack also makes the problem a lot similar to robust linear regression (probably in a high-dimensional space).

The experiment section is also confusing. In the theoretical analysis the main focus is on regression, but the tasks considered in the experiment section is effectively classification tasks. How could results on classification tasks verify guarantees for regression tasks? The dataset halfmoon is a mystery: "Halfmoon is a randomly generated 2D synthetic dataset". How did you generate it? What is the label and feature? How are they related? I could not find them either in the main body or appendix. 

Comparison with KNN exclusively is also misleading. What is so special about KNN? In terms of certifiable robustness, the natural choice of comparison is (ReLU) network. As Laplacian regression aims at data with graphical structure, I would also consider ML models specifically designed for that kind of data (e.g., graph neural networks). Highlighting "better than KNN" does not make sense to me. 

The paper writing is also sloppy. There is obvious typo even in the abstract ("There is great interest": either "great interests" or "a great interest"). The flow of the abstract and introduction is not smooth. Section 3 is awkward: it is less than a page, claims to be "COMPLEXITY ANALYSIS"  but only has a table showing empirical runtime comparison between KNN and Laplacian regression.  In fact, the logic for section 3 is confusing: Is this paper about "computational advantages of Laplacian regression over KNN"? Why should one care about Table 2 at all?

Overall, understanding adversarial attacks on graph-oriented ML models like Laplacian regression may be desired, but this paper does not motivate, address and present the problem in a convincing way.
content.rating: 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection
content.confidence: 3: The reviewer is fairly confident that the evaluation is correct

display_title: Looks solid but should be made clearer

content.title: Looks solid but should be made clearer
content.review:
This paper investigates adversarial robustness Graph Laplacian based semi-supervised learning from a theoretical view. 

My concerns are listed as below:

- This paper is highly dependent on Wang et al. (2018b) addressing adversarial robustness of nearest neighbor classifiers. The problem is that kNN is an inductive model, while GL-based semi-supervised learning is a transductive model. In these two cases, evasion attacks differ quite a lot. It should be made clear in the GL-based semi-supervised learning case how the adversarial perturbation on the unlabeled data affect the graph construction.
- The paper lacks some references [1, 2] which could be very relevant with the theoretical analysis and experiments.
- To evaluate robustness of general machine learning models, strong hard-label black box attacks should be used such as [3, 4, 5].

[1] Robustness for Non-Parametric Methods: A Generic Attack and Defense.
Yao-Yuan Yang, Cyrus Rashtchian, Yizhen Wang and Kamalika Chaudhuri. AISTATS, 2020.
[2] When are Non-Parametric Methods Robust? Robi Bhattacharjee and Kamalika Chaudhuri. ICML, 2020.
[3] Decision-Based Adversarial Attacks: Reliable Attacks Against Black-Box Machine Learning Models. Wieland Brendel, Jonas Rauber, Matthias Bethge. ICLR, 2018.
[4] Query-Efficient Hard-label Black-box Attack: An Optimization-based Approach , Minhao Cheng, Thong Le, Pin-Yu Chen, Huan Zhang, Jinfeng Yi, Cho-Jui Hsieh. ICLR, 2019.
[5] Sign-OPT: A Query-Efficient Hard-label Adversarial Attack , Minhao Cheng, Simranjit Singh, Patrick H. Chen, Pin-Yu Chen, Sijia Liu, Cho-Jui Hsieh. ICLR, 2020.
content.confidence: 2: The reviewer is willing to defend the evaluation, but it is quite likely that the reviewer did not understand central parts of the paper

content.title: Thank you for your review
content.comment: We thank the reviewers for reviewing our paper. After careful consideration, we think our paper is inappropriate for ICLR, and we decided to withdraw our paper.
